messages:
kevin: Heads-up, node gpu-node-112 hit repeated Xid 79s during a customer load test. Noticed automatic drain kicked in but node came back into service (we saw more errors after relabel).

maria: Ugh. Do we have nvml/ECC counters around that time?

gpu-bot: Alert: gpu-node-112 - Xid 79 GPU error observed (3 occurrences in 7m). Logged by node-monitor/driver-watcher. Link: https://internal.redwood/alerts/1769456789

ajay: I pulled the logs. kernel shows PCIe AER resets + Xid 79; driver stacktrace points at tpc/memcopy. Attached nvml snapshot: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.uncorrected,retired_pages --format=csv` shows a small uptick but not conclusive.

sre-oncall: Can we reproduce with a soak? If it's flaky we should burn it under stress for 12h before deciding replace/repair.

kevin: Proposal: run a focused soakbench flow I sketched: 1) cordon & drain node, 2) run soakbench with combined memory+compute workload (matrix mul, large batch inference, nvme stress), 3) collect nvml logs + system metrics, 4) if Xid > 0 re-run with PCIe stress and power cycling, 5) if still flaky open RMA. Thoughts?

maria: +1. Add a step to toggle ECC off/on and repeat (some flaky DIMMs show correlation). Also capture `dmesg --follow` during the run.

qa-lead: For reproducibility, we need a short run config that usually triggers the issue within 2-4h and a long run for up to 24h. I'll contribute input pairs and pass/fail criteria.

ajay: I created a new soak profile: `soakbench run --profile=mem-heavy --duration=4h --gpu-stress=cuda-matrix --collect=nvml,dmesg,pcie`

opsbot: ran: `fleetctl exec --node gpu-node-112 -- sudo kubectl drain gpu-node-112 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` (ok)

kevin: Commands we used / recommend:
```
# collect ECC counters
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,ecc.errors.corrected.volatile,ecc.errors.uncorrected.volatile --format=csv -l 30 > /tmp/nvml-ecc.csv &
# realtime kernel logs
journalctl -k -f > /tmp/dmesg-tail.log &
# run cuda stress (open-source harness)
./cuda-stress --gpu 0 --matrix-size 16384 --iters 100000
```

maria: Also: run PCIe exerciser: `pcie-stress --duration 2h --link-train` and `smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1` to rule out storage triggering resets.

ajay: Prometheus queries I used to spot pre-failure trend: `rate(node_dmesg_messages{job="node-exporter"} [5m])` and `increase(nvidia_gpu_xid_errors_total[1h])`. Dashboard card: GPU Xid histogram over 24h.

kevin: After 2h of mem-heavy soakbench we got one Xid 79 and a PCIe AER reset entry. Not a full repro but enough to keep it out of rotation.

sre-oncall: Policy decision: for single ephemeral Xid + warm reboot fixes => mark node as "quarantined" and schedule 24h soak. For >3 Xid in 24h => replace. We should codify into `fleetctl` automation.

maria: I'll add a small automation in CI: `soak-run` job that attaches to drained nodes and posts a short verdict back to Slack with logs link. Pseudocode:
```
if Xid_count >= 3 then verdict = "replace" else if Xid_count == 1 then verdict = "quarantine-24h" else verdict = "pass" fi
post_slack(channel=eng-infra, verdict, artifacts)
```

qa-lead: For handoff to hardware vendor, export `nvml` snapshots + `dmesg` and include step-by-step reproduction notes. They ask for the exact command lines and durations.

kevin: Note to triage: some cards only fail under mixed host and device mem pressure (large host->device transfers at high concurrency). If you only run pure GPU kernels you might miss it. Use inference-style loads (batch=256 seq=2048) to emulate customer traffic.

ajay: We also saw node-level thermal spikes ~78C preceding one failure. Not sure if cause or effect. We should collect `lm-sensors` and power draw from BMC.

opsbot: soakbench run complete (4h). Artifacts uploaded: https://internal.artifacts/soak/gpu-node-112/1769456789.tar.gz

maria: Quick verdict from artifacts: 1 Xid 79, 2 AER resets, thermal spike 78C, nvml shows 1 retired page. I'm leaning toward RMA unless long-soak is clean.

sre-oncall: Doing long soak (24h mem+pcie stress). I'll schedule it tonight and update tomorrow morning.

kevin: Thanks all. If long soak fails, ops to triage RMA with vendor and assign replacement node from spare pool. If clean, we run ECC toggle + 24h read-only soak before returning to service. :thumbsup:

gpu-bot: Reminder: recording incident notes to infra/triangle so we have history for this GPU serial.

ajay: Logging checklist for the thread so we don't miss artifacts: nvml-csv, dmesg-tail.log, journalctl -u nvidia-driver, pci-aer.log, lm-sensors, bmc-power.log, soakbench config.json, kubectl describe node output.

qa-lead: I'll post a short howto for oncall with one-click commands for soak runs and artifact upload.

kevin: Leaving this thread open until long-soak completes (ETA ~1769460400). If anyone reruns tests, paste results here.

sre-oncall: Long-soak started. Will ping with verdict. :white_check_mark:
